layers.message: Retry webhook deliveries with exponential backoff
Show report totals and averages with two decimals
Read port and webhook URL from the environment

graderOnly: No baseline or comparison range is recorded anywhere: STATE.md is the fresh installed brownfield state with no active cycle (Active Work.Id UNSET), there are no cycle records, and the working tree is clean.

History on the single checked-out branch is: Initial project; Add monthly summary report; the STANDARDS installation commit; Retry webhook deliveries with exponential backoff (src/webhooks/deliver.js, test/deliver.test.js); Show report totals and averages with two decimals (src/reports/summary.js, test/summary.test.js); Read port and webhook URL from the environment (src/config.js, src/app.js, test/config.test.js, package.json). The three most recent commits touch unrelated areas, so 'this change' could plausibly mean the last commit, any one of them, everything since the installation, or the installation itself.

The current code is fully readable: deliver() retries 5xx responses and thrown errors up to 4 attempts with delays 200, 400, 800 ms and does not retry statuses below 500; summarize() returns count, total and average as two-decimal strings; loadConfig(env) reads PORT and WEBHOOK_URL with defaults 8080 and http://localhost:9000/hooks; createNotifier(send, env) uses loadConfig.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture for a Navigator 'what did this change do' question with no recorded baseline. 00-project (pre-install) commits a small Node notifier: webhook delivery (single attempt), static config, app wiring, delivery tests. 05-report (pre-install) adds a summary report with an unformatted total. The builder then installs STANDARDS (default brownfield state, no active cycle, no records). 50-retry, 51-report-format and 52-config are three unrelated post-install commits (retry with backoff; two-decimal totals plus average; environment-driven config). The working tree is left clean and only one branch exists, so the plausible ranges are HEAD~1..HEAD, any single recent commit, the install commit onward, or the full history; nothing records which one the user means. Current code is self-explanatory, so a correct run can explain current behavior while asking which change/range is meant.
